newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Rwanda returns plane to new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda returns plane to new Congo.

text.p: The Democratic Republic of the Congo on Wednesday got back a plane which had been grounded in the Rwandan town of Kamembe for more than a year, state television reported.

Now-ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's government said at the time that bad weather forced the pilot, who was flying in Zaire, now renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo, from Kinshasa to Bukavu, to make an emergency landing across the Rwandan border in Kamembe.

But Tutsi-dominated authorities in the Rwandan capital Kigali said this was untrue and that there were weapons on the flight that were being sent to Hutu militiamen who had launched cross-border attacks against Tutsis inside Rwanda.
They grounded the plane and released the more than 30 passengers unharmed.

"There is good news for travellers. The aeroplane of Air Congo (the national airline) which was long kept in Rwanda is back home," the television said. The return of the plane followed negotiations between officials of the two countries, it said.

Rwandan soldiers were seen in the ranks of Laurent Kabila's Alliance forces who drove Mobutu from power in May after seven months of bush war. Rwanda's vice-president and strongman Paul Kagame is on good terms with the new president of the vast central African country.
Air Congo is virtually bankrupt after years of mismanagement. The company now only has one plane -- the one returned home from Kamembe.
Many of the airline's employees have not received their meagre salaries for more than two years.
